body:
`_run_one` runs every gate command captured (`template/src/pdca_harness/gates.py:410`), `_classify` keeps only the **last output line** (`gates.py:423`), and the row truncates that to **120 characters** (`gates.py:419`). The full stdout+stderr is then dropped. `check-gates.json` / `check-gates.md` are the only record a gate run leaves, so the entire evidence for a verdict — including a *gating* red that parks the bundle — is one truncated line.

## Measured

getwyrd/wyrd-pdca `issue_648`, 2026-07-31. The 7th round's `C4-ci` (the one gating correctness row) recorded:

```
xtask: `cargo test --workspace --exclude wyrd-dst` failed with exit status: 101
```

- All six archived iterations of the same bundle had this row **green**.
- Re-running the identical command in the identical, untouched worktree hours later: **green, exit 0** — the failure was transient.
- **Which test failed is unrecoverable.** The output existed once, in the capture pipe, and nothing wrote it anywhere.

The post-mortem had to be reconstructed from side effects: the verify worktree's reflog stamps and target-dir mtimes bound the failing run to under ~90 seconds of a test step that takes ~7 minutes green, i.e. it died in one of the first test binaries. That archaeology is exactly what a log file would replace — and it still could not name the test.

The row's 120-char evidence line is the right *summary*; the defect is that it is also the entire *record*.

## Suggested shape

- A bundle-scoped gate run writes `gate-logs/<rule_id>.log` into the bundle: a small header (command, cwd, `$PDCA_WORKTREE`, start time, duration, exit code / outcome), then the combined output verbatim. One file per rule id, overwritten per Check run; the iterate archive moves the directory alongside `DOWNSTREAM_GLOBS`, so each round keeps its own evidence.
- The row gains `log` (bundle-relative path) and `duration_secs`, additively — no existing consumer reads either key.
- On timeout, `run_with_heartbeat` attaches the partial capture to the `TimeoutExpired` it raises (the exception type carries an `output` field already), so a hung gate's log shows *where* it hung instead of nothing.
- A repo-scoped run with no bundle (`pdca gates --working-tree`, the CI re-gate) can keep today's behaviour — CI has its own console.

A rendered instance (getwyrd/wyrd-pdca) is staging this locally, pending upstream.
title: gates: a gate's full output is discarded — a red gating row keeps 120 chars of its last line, so a one-off failure is undiagnosable
